ssoCapacity.method: Mean of published sun-synchronous capacity ÷ leoCapacityKg for Electron (200 ÷ 300 = 0.67), Firefly Alpha (630 ÷ 1000 = 0.63) and PSLV (1750 ÷ 3800 = 0.46): 0.59, rounded to 0.6. The script applies it to every picked rocket that has no ssoCapacityKg override.

include.why: Smallest dedicated launcher: cheap, small capacity

sources.source: Rocket Lab, Electron Payload User's Guide 7.0
sources.note: Quoted for a 500 km sun-synchronous orbit. The same guide gives up to 300 kg to lower orbits, which matches leoCapacityKg. Read from search-engine copies of the guide, because Rocket Lab's site refuses automated access; still to be confirmed in a browser (TODO T3).

sources.source: Firefly Aerospace, Alpha vehicle page, Performance section

manual.name: Rideshare (shared launch)

sources.source: SpaceX Smallsat Rideshare Program, online price tool: price for 2026 flights to sun-synchronous orbit
sources.note: $350,000 for up to 50 kg, then $7,000 for each extra kg. The price depends on the flight year; this is the 2026 price. Read from search-engine copies of the tool's result pages, because the tool needs a browser; still to be confirmed in a browser (TODO T3).

A 200 kg limit, a 98% success rate, a reusable rocket and a fixed 525 km sun-synchronous orbit (the orbit is on the mission card, design.md section 4.3). Both capacity fields hold the same limit, because this option only flies to its fixed orbit.

manual.note: Not from Launch Library 2. The player cannot choose the orbit. The launch price is launchCostUsd for a satellite of up to includedKg, plus costPerKgUsd for each kg above that.
